items.text: A third US aircraft carrier, the [[p:USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71)|USS Theodore Roosevelt]], has reached the Middle East, according to Axios and Israel's Channel 12 citing a US official. That puts more than 20,000 US sailors and Marines in the region as the war with Iran passes seven months.
items.outlet: The Times of Israel (citing Axios, Channel 12)
items.notes: Arrival rests on an unnamed US official; link2 covers the deployment, not the arrival.

items.text: The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] navy says two more oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz while using an 'unauthorised' route with tracking switched off. It also claims to have shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island. Neither claim has been independently verified, and US Central Command has disputed earlier IRGC mine claims.
items.notes: IRGC claims only; no ship names given.

items.text: The [[p:ASEAN]] summit opened in Manila for three days, with the Middle East war and its economic fallout at the top of the agenda. A draft statement stresses peaceful settlement of disputes and freedom of navigation in the South China Sea. Chinese Premier [[p:Li Qiang]] meets ASEAN leaders on Monday and leaves before [[p:Donald Trump]] arrives on Tuesday for a [[p:Quadrilateral Security Dialogue|Quad]] meeting, a US–ASEAN summit and talks with [[p:Bongbong Marcos]].

Estonia will close all three of its border crossings with Russia from 1 Dec, Foreign Minister [[p:Margus Tsahkna]] announced, after an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems' plant in Viimsi near Tallinn early on 14 Nov. Tsahkna says there is 'clear evidence' that Russia's [[p:GRU (Russian Federation)|GRU]] ordered it; eight people living in Latvia were detained. Moscow called the move Russophobic if confirmed.
items.notes: Closure confirmed by the foreign minister; whether it is temporary or indefinite is for the government to decide. GRU role is Estonia's attribution.

items.text: Traffic on the Crimean Bridge was halted overnight after a Ukrainian attack, the fourth on the bridge since 2022; Crimea's Russian-installed head [[p:Sergey Aksyonov]] said restrictions would last until about midday. Russia's defence ministry claims it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones over 17 regions that night. On 15 Nov Ukraine's General Staff said it hit the TAIF-NK refinery and the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant in Tatarstan, a helicopter maker in Bryansk Oblast and an airfield in Astrakhan Oblast.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Bridge damage not stated; drone count is Russia's claim; strike results are Ukrainian claims.

items.text: After the Abu Dhabi round and his meetings with Putin and Zelenskyy, [[p:Jared Kushner]] said Washington's focus is now on 'facilitating direct engagement' between Moscow and European partners while it prepares the next three-way round. He called [[p:NATO]] a 'critical pillar' of credible guarantees for Ukraine and said several new ideas were being explored.
items.notes: Based on Kushner's own post on X; no date set for the next round.

items.text: Ombudsman [[p:Dmytro Lubinets]] says Kyiv and Moscow agreed weekly evacuations of vulnerable civilians, such as older and sick people, from occupied areas, with help from the [[p:International Committee of the Red Cross|ICRC]]; 16 people came back on 12 Nov. Zelenskyy separately rejected Putin's proposed 'humanitarian mission' in Kostiantynivka as a ploy to take the city, where fighting continues.
items.notes: Evacuation deal is a Ukrainian official's account; no Russian confirmation found.

items.text: Zelenskyy says a 161 km/h speed cap on Starshield, the military version of [[p:Starlink]], over the front and occupied areas hampers interceptor drones hunting Shaheds and leaves substations exposed. He told officials to resolve it with Washington and [[p:SpaceX]], which told Axios there has been 'no change'. The Congressional Ukraine Caucus demanded an explanation.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Kyiv's claim; SpaceX denies a change. Who imposed the cap is unclear.

items.text: Oleh Apostol, commander of Ukraine's air assault forces, says Russia's advance has slowed sharply and that Ukraine retook more than 800 km² in two operations. Ukraine's General Staff put Russian casualties in October at 54,400, its highest monthly figure of the war. Fighting continues inside Kostiantynivka, which Russia claims to hold.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Ukrainian military claims; ISW's October estimate of a small Russian net loss is consistent in direction.

items.text: Russian strikes kept hitting cities and the grid: 50 people were hurt in a Zaporizhzhia apartment block on 13 Nov, at least 7 were killed and 80 injured nationwide on 14 Nov, and a 'mass attack' on Odesa Oblast on 15 Nov hit a DTEK energy site and cut power to about 41,000 families. Ukraine's air force counted 132 drones that night, 78 of them jet-powered.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes

items.text: Drones struck three merchant ships off Romania's Black Sea coast near Sulina over two days: the Palau-flagged Larissa 1 on 13 Nov, then the Greek-flagged tanker Evia Petrol V and the bulk carrier Marsol on 14 Nov, both of which caught fire. No one was hurt. Romania has not identified where the drones came from and scrambled two F-16s.
items.notes: Origin of drones not established; Romanian defence minister says an investigation is under way.

items.text: A drone that entered Lithuania from Belarus overnight on 10–11 Nov crossed all three Baltic states into Russia after NATO jets twice failed to shoot it down near Biržai. Its origin is unknown; officials floated the idea that Russian jamming diverted a Ukrainian drone. President [[p:Gitanas Nausėda]] called it a 'restless and difficult' night, with suspected balloons too.
items.notes: Thread fit is provisional: origin unknown.
